text.p: Italian debt markets charged ahead in late European trade, beating new high after new high on the front month futures contract and sucking the BTP-Bund spread in to a record degree.
"Convergence -- that's the password," said one broker at a London-based futures brokerage.
"Now everyone's convinced that Maastricht is right around the corner and they're behaving accordingly," another said.
The September BTp future on LIFFE galloped up to a record peak of 133.33 in after-hours trade, standing 73 basis points up on the day. The February 2007 Btp ended 36 bps up at 99.20.
The Feb07 was yielding 6.97 percent and the spread over the benchmark Bund narrowed to a record of 124 basis points.
"The fact that this morning the market didn't go down put fear into people who had stayed out or gone short," a broker said.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a newspaper interview earlier he saw no reason why the Btp-Bund spread should not stand at 60-70 basis points like in Spain.
Dealers cited plenty of foreign buyers and added that if Italy was really going to converge, the spread should arrive at 100 basis points, which was 134-135 on the future.
Others were more cautious, noting that it still was not entirely clear how a dispute between the German government and the Bundesbank over revaluing gold reserves would be settled.
